requestsPrev.txt: Children's Justice Centers are statutorily mandated to provide forensic, treatment, and advocacy services to child abuse victims and their families. They serve approximately 20,000 individuals annually. The requested $470,000 will ensure access by providing funding to cover cuts to personnel, service contracts, and related operations largely resulting from federal grant cuts, reductions in other funding sources, and inflationary increases.

NEMT membership declines in Utah have driven annual losses of over $2 million since 2023. At the current $2.01 per member per month capitated rate, projected losses average $2.2 million annually over the next three years. The decrease in m

requestsPrev.name: Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (HAR0046)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This appropriation will establish a Medicaid reimbursement for Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT) under CPT 81420 without prior authorization. These services are currently covered by 49 of 51 State Medicaid programs, so this appropriation will bring Utah's Medicaid into alignment with the industry standard across the country. NIPT is a simple blood test that screens for chromosomal aneuploidies to inform diagnostic testing and to assist in family planning and appropriate labor and delivery procedures.

requestsPrev.name: Opioid Use Disorder Treatment at Community Health Centers (HAR0065)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: Eight of Utah's community health centers (Carbon Medical Service Association, Inc., Community Health Centers, Inc., Creek Valley Health Clinic, Family Healthcare, Fourth Street Clinic, Mountainlands Family Health Center, Utah Partners for Health and Wayne Community Health Center) are requesting $1.3 million in opioid settlement funds to continue their OUD treatment programs in rural and underserved communities, which were expanded beginning in 2023 with the support of opioid settlement funds. This level of funding would allow 8 health centers operating in 15 counties to continue to provide OUD

requestsPrev.name: Opioid Use Disorder Treatment Protocol Pilot Program (HAR0129)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: OUD Management Partners (OUDMP), a Utah-based company, has developed a unique protocol that has successfully treated roughly 4,000 OUD clinic patients. This proprietary approach involves daily interaction between patients and medical professionals. Utilizing an app-based telehealth platform, the program is designed to reach OUD patients anywhere and everywhere. OUDMP would like to partner with the state in conducting a pilot program reaching key affected demographics.

requestsPrev.name: Pro-life Utah Support Life Program (HAR0071)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: Funding granted to a nonprofit organization in Utah, to expand a program to enhance and increase resources that promote childbirth instead of abortion to women facing unplanned pregnancies and to offer services, including pregnancy support services, parenting help and adoption assistance.

requestsPrev.name: Recovery Community Centers (HAR0067)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This Funding will be used to support programs that are dedicated to the fitness, health, and wellness of people in recovery that were most directly impacted by the opioid epidemic. Fit to Recover and the School of Addiction Recovery provide an array of services and establish a supportive community for people in recovery from SUDs. These programs enhance quality of life and increase the likelihood of participants achieving long-term recovery.

requestsPrev.name: Senior Recreation Services (HAR0020)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This funding request is to support the development and enhancement of the Riverdale Senior Center, a regional center, ensuring it can meet the growing demand for services, programs, and social engagement opportunities. Investing in this facility will promote health, independence, and quality of life for aging citizens, while also reducing long-term healthcare and social service costs.

requestsPrev.name: Specialized Supports Massage Therapy (HAR0056)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This is a request to adjust the Medicaid reimbursement rate for specialized massage from $15.29 to $25.00. The current recommended rate is $32.50. The ongoing funding request would be $452,045.46. Specialized Supports Massage is a medically prescribed, DSPD-authorized service that supports individuals with severe disabilities who experience chronic pain, muscle spasticity, neurological impairment, and related functional limitations.

requestsPrev.name: Statewide Sexual Assault Helpline (HAR0066)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: Asking for $300,000 of ongoing state funding for the 24/7 Statewide Sexual Assault helplines available in both English and Spanish. These helplines provide immediate (free and confidential) support and resources to victims, professionals, law enforcement and families who have been affected by sexual violence.

requestsPrev.name: Strengthening Family Resilience After Loss (HAR0122)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This RFA requests one time funding for the Utah Department of Health and Human Services to support the Strengthening Family Resilience After Loss initiative. This appropriation will sustain and modestly expand an early-intervention pilot program that connects children and families to critical supports following the death of a parent or caregiver. requestsPrev.name: Supporting Clinicians in Providing Childhood Screenings (HAR0130)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: The requested funding would allow for Medicaid reimbursement to providers through CPT codes for validated trauma screenings, including ACEs. The funding would be utilized over the next 1-3 years to pilot test provider reimbursement, which would gather data to improve early detection and response to childhood trauma in Utah. We have partners providing the clinician training including U of U, UPIQ, Primary Children's, and Intermountain Health who are each investing up to $500k per year. With ACEs Resource Network investing $680k each year for 3 years and GenerationAll supporting with $900k, tota

requestsPrev.name: Sustaining Special Education - Infants and Toddlers (SAR0095)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: 4.5 million ongoing request. This appropriation will support children, from birth to age three, with disabilities and developmental delays. Funding for the Baby Watch Early Intervention program, (Special Education for infants and toddlers), has not sustained the needed services. The per visit reimbursement rate has remained flat since 2017 causing high caseloads and increased turnover. Early Intervention helps these children catch back up to their same-aged peers before they enter school and have a need for Pre K-12 Special Education services.

requestsPrev.name: Take 100 people off of the DSPD waiting list (HAR0126)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This request would provide funding to serve 100 individuals with the most acute disability needs at the top of the DSPD waiting list.

requestsPrev.name: Utah Health Artificial Intelligence Vault (UHAIV) (SAR0080)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This request is for funding to support the development of the Utah Health AI Vault by modernizing the Utah Population Database to accelerate discovery, improve outcomes, and drive economic growth. This would be housed at the University of Utah and support the development of a new technology system to utilize data and AI to support population-based medical and policy decisions.

requestsPrev.name: Utah Health Care Transparency (SAR0057)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: This request funds One Utah Health Collaborative to provide independent, data-driven analysis using the Utah All Payer Claims Database, data from stakeholders and other state data assets to measure total health care spending growth and identify primary cost drivers attributable to price and utilization. The project will improve transparency of emergency department utilization, including inappropriate use, and support provider organization and health system level performance analysis. This will include specific services level price information to enable employer and consumer engagement in choic

requestsPrev.name: Utah Youth Mental Health Resources (HAR0138)
requestsPrev.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
requestsPrev.txt: 1.3 Funding Request Description: Requesting $20 million as a match to private donor funds to Huntsman Mental Health Foundation to increase mental health services to support youth, children, and families in Utah through Huntsman Mental Health Institute at the University of Utah. Child rates of anxiety, depression, and suicide per 100k residents are higher in Utah than U.S. averages, indicating greater demand relative to current system capacity. Services through Huntsman Mental Health Institute will be expanded to provide care and services to more youth. There is currently a gap in mental health

requestsPrev.name: Eliminating Insurance Fraud Pilot Program (SAR0066)
requestsPrev.txt: This request supports a one-year pilot deployment of secure patient self check-in kiosks with high-assurance Identity verification, Including peri-ocular biometric functionality, at University of Utah Health. The pilot is designed to prevent healthcare fraud, improper payments, and identity misuse driven by patient impersonation, inaccurate identity verification, and manual front-desk processes. By standardizing patient intake using secure kiosks that directly integrate with advanced, non-generative, healthcare-specific analytical systems for claims and billing validation, along with digital c

requestsPrev.name: Aspen Center for Learning (HAR0058)
requestsPrev.txt: The Aspen Center for Learning is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization created to provide continuing educational opportunities for post-high school students with special needs. Aspen is requesting funding to build a pilot program with Utah Valley University and to help construct a learning center on donated land in Heber City. Millions of dollars have been raised from parents of these individuals and the public to build the center, and we are asking the State of Utah to also participate in helping to fill this social gap for our vulnerable citizens. The total project is estimated to cost $11 mill

requestsPrev.name: Capital Improvements for Fellowship Hall (HAR0042)
requestsPrev.txt: This request seeks funding for structural improvements to the facility owned and operated by the Fellowship Foundation of Utah. This Foundation provides a facility for 12-Step Recovery for all kinds of addiction. Proposed improvements include a new roof, parking lot renovations, HVAC upgrades, and kitchen improvements.

requestsPrev.name: Comprehensive Victim Service Campus Expansion (SAR0084)
requestsPrev.txt: The requested $7.5 million will help construct a new victim services campus in Utah County for "The Refuge Utah", including a larger domestic violence safehouse, a victim advocacy center, and transitional housing. The expansion will increase capacity from 25 beds up to 138 beds, filling the gap in need for additional safe shelter and trauma-informed services while allowing for future growth. The current safehouse and rape crisis center facilities have not expanded at the same rate as the growing population, and last year alone 451 safehouse requests went unmet due to limited capacity. The new

requestsPrev.name: Fourth Street Clinic Capital Project (HAR0014)
requestsPrev.txt: This appropriations request will support the construction of a new homeless health center, owned and operated by Wasatch Homeless Healthcare, doing business as the Fourth Street Clinic. Fourth Street Clinic has over 35 years of providing integrated healthcare services to individuals experiencing homelessness and serves a vital role in Salt Lake County to prevent unnecessary emergency room utilization and hospitalizations among the most vulnerable in our community. The new space will support expanded capacity in medical, behavioral health, dental, and pharmacy while increasing the total number

requestsPrev.name: Loan for Land Purchase for Trail Connectivity (HAR0031)
requestsPrev.txt: Purchase of property necessary to connect trail system near Utah State University and the island part of Logan City at approximately 400 N and 600 E in Logan, Utah. The land and existing residential dwellings will be purchased with loaned funds. The loan will be repaid from the subsequent sale of restructured properties.

requestsPrev.name: Prison Capacity Expansion (HAR0013)
requestsPrev.txt: Funding would support prison expansion to address significant increases in various prison populations that are approaching critical levels in the near term - as soon as 2027. Under current trend If these populations go unaddressed, the Department of Corrections may need to make determinations including early release of offenders. Even if construction begins immediately, it would take at least a few years to open to house any inmates.

requestsPrev.name: Rocky Mountain Global Peace & Sports Complex (RMGPS) (SAR0105)
requestsPrev.txt: Construction of a multi-ADD sport and educational campus in Wasatch County/ This facility provides critical infrastructure to resolve Utah's youth sports ice/field deficit and could serve as a primary training hub for the 2034 Olympic mandate.

requestsPrev.name: Sober Living Expansion (HAR0041)
requestsPrev.txt: Valley Behavioral Health, "Valley", is seeking $1.0 million from Utah's Opioid Settlement Fund to purchase an existing building with 15-20 rooms/units in Salt Lake County with the intention to convert it to sober living/ transitional housing. Using these funds to support individuals seeking recovery and sobriety is aligned with Utah's values and fills a gap of sober living units in the county.

requestsPrev.name: Union Station Intermodal Entry Improvements (SAR0069)
requestsPrev.txt: This request supports targeted entryway and interface improvements at Ogden Union Station to enable its full function as Northern Utah's primary intermodal transportation and civic hub. The project focuses on improving how passengers and visitors arrive, orient, transfer between modes, and access downtown Ogden through the Station. These improvements align with statewide transit investments and reinforce Union Station's role as a historic, cultural, and transportation gateway. The project will help solidify Ogden as the downtown and central gathering place for Northern Utah while preserving th

requestsPrev.name: Improving Home Purchasing Power for All Utahns (HAR0040)
requestsPrev.txt: This program aims to strengthen and support all families, especially low-to-moderate income individuals, families, and communities by teaching them how to apply sound money management skills through customized education and services. It is a multi-faceted program designed to improve lender credit scores quickly and efficiently, using personalized, data-driven insights.

requestsPrev.name: Central Wasatch Mountain Projects -- Millcreek Canyon (SAR0002)
requestsPrev.txt: The RFA includes funding for the CWC's essential canyon project work including canyon graffiti abatement, the Ski Bus Priority Access program, trailhead bathroom maintenance, and the CWC's community grant program that funds needed infrastructure and education programming.

requestsPrev.name: OLYMPIC AUTOMATED TRANSIT PILOT (HAR0094)
requestsPrev.txt: Future-forward transportation is here. The Olympic Automated Transit Pilot aims to land and scale an autonomous public transit fleet, operational by the 2034 Olympics. This public-private partnership is a 3-year structured rollout with two lanes: 1) UTA will build a mixed autonomous fleet comprised of platooning buses & robotaxis and 2) Utah will attract private automated vehicle network services (robotaxis) through regulatory sandbox and strategic incentives. The project will secure federal grants and private partnerships to amplify impact far beyond state-only investment. We want Utah to do

requestsPrev.name: Pando Tree Utah Highway 25 Signage Project (HAR0012)
requestsPrev.txt: Each year, thousands of visitors come to visit and enjoy the Pando Tree, some 11,000 in 2025 alone. It is estimated those visitors conservatively spend $40 a day, generating $27,084 in state tax revenues. Today, the State Highway, (UT Hwy 25) lacks signage to help visitors to get where there is adequate parking, information, and facilities to help folks visit and enjoy this Utah wonder. UDOT Region 4, Fishlake National Forest, and Friends of Pando has collaborated on a plan to install highway signage (attached). The total cost for the project is $4,454.04. Fishlake National Forest and Friends

requestsPrev.name: Spanish Fork Airport Taxiway Bravo Construction (SAR0103)
requestsPrev.txt: This request is for $3.5 million to complete the second taxiway (Taxiway Bravo) of KSPK, the Spanish Fork Airport. This project has received federal funding from the FAA and direct appropriations from Congressman Owens. The total project is $10 million. We are asking for the final $3.5 million.

requestsPrev.name: St. George Regional Airport Terminal Expansion (SAR0009)
requestsPrev.txt: The City of St. George is requesting funds to support the expansion of the St. George Regional Airport terminal from three gates to seven. The total project cost is approximately $100 million, with the city contributing $21 million upfront. The remaining costs will be funded through a combination of bonding proceeds supported by County Tourism, Recreation, Cultural, and Convention (TRCC) revenues and contributions from SkyWest Airlines, and FAA funding.

requestsPrev.name: Union Station Intermodal Entry Improvements (SAR0069)
requestsPrev.txt: This request supports targeted entryway and interface improvements at Ogden Union Station to enable its full function as Northern Utah's primary intermodal transportation and civic hub. The project focuses on improving how passengers and visitors arrive, orient, transfer between modes, and access downtown Ogden through the Station. These improvements align with statewide transit investments and reinforce Union Station's role as a historic, cultural, and transportation gateway. The project will help solidify Ogden as the downtown and central gathering place for Northern Utah while preserving th

requestsPrev.name: Statewide Digital Instruction Platform (UEN) (HAR0045)
requestsPrev.txt: This request provides dedicated funding for a statewide digital instructional platform delivered and administered by the Utah Education Network (UEN). The platform is integrated into Utah's existing UEN-managed technology infrastructure and supports K-12 educators and students across the state. Funding this item separately allows UEN to continue operating and supporting the platform without placing other core statewide services at risk. The primary beneficiaries are Utah public school students and educators who rely on consistent, secure, and statewide access to instructional technology.

Sen. Owens commented on Brian Redd's great leadership, expressed appreciation, and emphasized continued support with the State and Salt Lake City.

Chair Brammer expressed appreciation and commented on the different and safer feeling of downtown Salt Lake City.

notes: Chair Stratton called the meeting to order at 8:09 a.m.
There were no minutes for approval.
8:10 Department of Health and Human Services' Operations Base budget
Sean Faherty introduced the Operations Base Budget for the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).
Chair Stratton invited the department to respond.
Nate Winters, Deputy Director, and Amanda Slater, Assistant Deputy Director, provided the response to the proposed cuts for DHHS.
Rep. Fiefia requested more information on staffing, and Nate Winters responded.
Rep. Ward moved to approve the following motions from the sheet entitled "Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee - Motions for Consideration": CA1, CA3 through CA8.
Rep. Ward moved to approve the following motions from the sheet entitled "Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee - Motions for Consideration": CB1 through CB16.
Sean Faherty continued the presentation, discussing the Oversight Budget.
Amanda Slater, Assistant Deputy Director, spoke to the proposed cuts.
Chair Stratton asked for additional information on background checks for providers, and Amanda Slater and Sean Faherty provided the information.
Rep. Fiefia asked what is the fee for a background check, and Amanda Slater, Nate Winters, and Russell Frandson responded.
Rep. Ward moved to approve the following motions from the sheet entitled "Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee - Motions for Consideration": CD1 through CD3.
8:30 Department of Health and Human Services' Children, Youth, and Families
Kevin Edminster explained the Children, Youth, and Families Base Budget.
Tonya Myrup, Director, Division of Child and Family Services, responded to the proposed budget reductions.
Rep. Dailey-Provost discussed the impact of not paying employees enough to keep them with the Division, and Tonya Myrup responded.
Rep. Fiefia asked how many workers would be cut, and Tonya Myrup responded.
Rep. Peck asked about the GRANDfamilies Kinship Program, and Tonya Myrup responded.
Rep. Fitisemanu asked if proposed reductions would impact federal matching funds, and Tonya Myrup responded.
Rep. Dailey-Provost requested the Division provide information on federal matching funds.
Rep. Gricius asked how a reduction in funds would impact training for foster parents, and Tonya Myrup responded.
Daniel Webster, Director of Operations, Utah Foster Care, was invited to tell the committee how the proposed reductions would impact the ability to provide foster care.
Rep. Gricius asked what impact the reductions would have on federal standards, and Daniel Webster responded.
Sen. Escamilla expressed concern with the impact that funding cuts would have on the State's liability.
Tonya Myrup and Brandy Naylor, Raise the Future, made a request for an appropriation for the adoption of Utah's longest-waiting children in foster care.
Tonya Myrup and Erin Jameson, Utah Domestic Violence Coalition, made the request for appropriations for victim services.
Noel Taxin, Director, Division of Family Health, made the appropriation request for Baby Watch Early Intervention Services.
Rep. Ward asked what would be the impact of budget cuts, and Noel Taxin responded.
Chair Stratton asked how long it has been since employees received a cost of living increase, and Noel Taxin responded.
Sen. Escamilla asked for information on maintenance of effort with the funds, and Kevin Edminster responded.
Rep. Chevrier asked if there is a flow chart showing all the programs for children, and Kevin Edminster replied.
Rep. Ward moved to approve the following motions from the sheet entitled "Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee - Motions for Consideration": CP1-CP4, CP5-CP10.

Kevin Edminster introduced the Base Budget for the Office of Recovery Services (ORS).
Georgia Wood, Division Director, discussed the review of ORS.
Georgia Wood discussed the ORS Ombuds program.
Kevin Edminster explained budget reduction options.
Rep. Jack moved to approve the following motions from the sheet entitled "Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee - Motions for Consideration": All #CQ1.

Kevin Edminster presented the Juvenile Justice and Youth Services (JJYS) Base Budget.
April Graham, Division Director, JJYS, provided a response to the proposed reductions.
Rep. Jack moved to approve the following motions from the sheet entitled "Social Services Appropriations Subcommittee - Motions for Consideration": All #CR1 and CR2.

Kevin Edminster discussed Correctional Health Services.
Marcus Wisner, Director, Division of Correctional Health Services, responded to the proposals.

Russell Frandsen explained the Fees Issue Brief.
Chair Stratton invited comment from subcommittee members on the agenda item, and no one responded.
Chair Stratton stated when public comment would be taken.
